problem: Prior topological-navigation and hierarchical RL methods depend on dense rewards, predefined landmarks/subgoals or handcrafted state spaces, so they explore inefficiently and generalize poorly in unknown, unstructured off-road environments with sparse extrinsic rewards.
motivation: Robots exploring unknown terrain without prior maps get little feedback, and flat RL or fixed-landmark topological maps do not cope. A map built online from detected landmarks, combined with hierarchical decisions and intrinsic rewards, could make exploration efficient and goal-directed.
key_idea: Build a topological map online from CBAM-attention-detected landmarks and let an H-DQN meta-controller pick map nodes as subgoals, trained with dense intrinsic and frontier-exploration rewards on top of sparse extrinsic rewards.
insight: Every component contributes. In the Scenario 1 ablation, removing the topological map drops SR from 98 to 88 and exploration coverage from 90 to 80. Removing the hierarchy is worst, with SR 85 and coverage 75, then removing attention with SR 86. So the hierarchy over map nodes matters most for sparse-reward navigation. The ablation is only on one scenario, and no ablation isolates the intrinsic-reward terms or landmark selection.
method: Attention-based feature detection: ResNet-50 with CBAM produces feature maps; a sliding window and ROI pooling give ROI features; a binary classifier scores landmark/object/tree presence, and each detection becomes a map node or subgoal.

Dynamic topological map: nodes hold feature vectors and edges hold traversability. A landmark is added if its similarity to existing nodes is below a threshold; if none is detected, a subgoal is generated along the trajectory at the max detection range.

Strategic landmark selection: candidates at similar distances are scored as w_N*exp(-lambda*visits) + w_GD*cosine(direction to landmark, direction to goal), and the highest score becomes the next subgoal.

Hierarchical H-DQN policy: a meta-controller Q-network picks subgoals from the map and per-subgoal sub-controller DQNs output primitive actions using the local obstacle map and kinematics. Each level has its own replay buffer and target network.

Composite reward: alpha*sparse extrinsic (goal/milestone) + beta*intrinsic (visit-count novelty, new subgoal, frontier-node, exploration-progress and uncertainty terms) + gamma*penalties (revisit, subgoal similarity, temporal non-exploration, obstacle collision).

Deployment: LiDAR point cloud plus Dynamic Window Approach for obstacle avoidance on a Clearpath Jackal; a subgoal-reachability theorem gives a 1-epsilon success bound, with epsilon = k*max epsilon_pq over k edges.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 + CBAM detector with H-DQN meta-controller/sub-controllers (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 1M steps in Unity 3D / ROS Noetic simulated off-road and outdoor terrains with a simulated Husky robot; no extra or web data
setting.observation: monocular RGB (AXIS camera) + 3D LiDAR point cloud (Velodyne)
setting.action_space: low-level primitive actions to reach subgoals, with DWA obstacle avoidance; high-level discrete topological-map node subgoals
setting.simulator: Unity 3D with ROS Noetic; real world for testing
setting.privileged: none stated; goal position is used for the goal-directedness score

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 episodes per environment, custom Unity and real off-road scenarios
numbers.extra: trained in simulation; evaluated over 100 episodes

numbers_note: Custom Unity and real-world scenarios, not a standard benchmark. Ablation numbers (Scenario 1) are in Table 2 and not repeated as entries. Baseline numbers are omitted.
results: TopoNav reaches SR 98/94/92 in scenarios 1/2/3, ahead of the strongest baseline LTVN (90/88/89). Navigation time falls to 30.6/33.8/35.1 s versus LTVN's 36.2/37.0/37.8 s, and coverage rises to 90/88/89 versus LTVN's 84/83/85. Abstract claims: coverage +7-20%, SR +9-19%, time -15-36%.
limitations: Scalability to large environments and long-horizon tasks is untested; large topological maps may be computationally costly.
Evaluation is on custom simulated/real scenarios with few baselines, no variance or statistical reporting, and the ablation covers only Scenario 1.
